newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit weaker on dlr covering,seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit weaker on dlr covering,seen under pressure.

text.p: * Ringgit weaker on short-covering of dollar positions
* Seen under pressure from offshore dollar demand
* Talk Bank Negara to sell dollar/ringgit at 2.5250
* Stop-loss orders for dollar/ringgit seen above 2.5270
The ringgit remained under pressure in early Asian trading due to short-covering of dollar positions by offshore players, dealers said.
But fears of intervention by Bank Negara were again capping the dollar's rise.
Dealers said there was talk that the central bank was waiting to sell the dollar at 2.5250, the level at which it had aggressively defended the ringgit.
"I think Negara is still there at 2.5250. That's why we are seeing a lot of selling (of dollar/ringgit) at just below that level," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Banking sources said the central bank had sold around $400 million last week to defend the ringgit.
On Friday, the ringgit weakened on rumours that Bank Negara would be holding meetings with local bank heads to discuss some possible restriction on ringgit lending to offshore players.
But banking sources said there was no such meeting.
At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5242/52 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5244/54 in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.

Dealers said though the ringgit was expected to remain under pressure from offshore dollar bids, its fall was likely to be limited by central bank intervention and corporate selling of the dollar out of Kuala Lumpur.
Further gains in dollar/ringgit could trigger stop-loss orders above the 2.5270 level, they said.
